seams: serverRun (manager.go:151-169) is already a per-process run object: proc, info, tracker, stopping/forced/ready, done/readyCh, cancelTail, cpu sample, discord status, events. It is the natural core of a per-instance struct. These Manager fields should move into that struct: job/jobCancel/loadWait, lastExit, crashes, known, lastPlayed, recs, idleSince (for per-game auto-stop), modVersions, a logs ring, its settings/paths and its library. App-wide parts stay on Manager: activity feed, history/byPlayers (machine), discord sender, net, checks, app update, waker, keepAwakeUntil/wakeHold.

runInfo (manager.go:173-201) is the persisted run record. It can become a RunRecord superset with game/instance id and adapter extras such as keeper port/token or RCON port, all omitempty. runtime.json stays Valheim's, and other instances get their own file. The adoption algorithm in adoptRunning (run file → OpenProc → ±2 s start-time check → FindByExe, server.go:503-522) is generic. The adapter only has to give the run-file path and a process matcher (exe path, or exe plus cmdline/cwd for java/dotnet).

The job machinery (jobs.go: Job, jobCtl.step/result/setCancellable, ActionError with Action, BusyError, errCancelled) is game-neutral. Only the single slot needs to change: one slot per instance plus an app slot (waker, app update), and Job gains an omitempty instance/game field. The Action strings ('install', 'settings', 'worlds', 'log', 'force_stop') need an instance context.

steamcmd.Installer (steamcmd.go:43-46: Install(ctx, validate, progress)), the optional SetInstallDir (settings.go:85-87) and Options.NewInstaller(config.Paths) (manager.go:52) form the install seam. Per game it would be SteamCMD with an app id, or HTTP download (Mojang jar, Terraria zip, Vintage Story tarball), plus a runtime install (Java/.NET). An installed check and a build/version query (today steamcmd.InstalledBuild in status.go:158) belong with it.

The process seam is platform.Proc (Interrupt/Kill/Wait/Exited/Usage/PID/StartTime) with StartDetached, OpenProc and FindByExe. doStop (server.go:350-415) hard-codes Interrupt, 90 s resend and 4 min timeout. It should run an adapter-defined stop chain (console line via keeper → RCON/REST → Ctrl+C/SIGINT → kill) with the adapter's timeouts and a 'saved' signal. ForceStop (server.go:101-129) stays generic.

logparse's game-neutral output is Activity (Kind join/leave/death/online/saved/wrong_password/bad_version/load_failed/bad_password_config, Name, PlatformID, Text; tracker.go:18-25) plus records.Event. Tracker's generic surface can become an interface: Apply(ev, now) []Activity, Players, Count, Ready, LastSave, Stopping/StoppingAt, Version, Reset, Overdue, KnownPlatformID. The Valheim-only JoinCode, PublicAddr, CrossplayFailed and NoJoinCode go into a Valheim join extension. The adapter supplies IsNoise, Parse/NewTracker, the timestamp format, and where the log comes from: a file passed by argument (Valheim), a file the game picks (Minecraft logs/latest.log), or stdout captured by the keeper.

The tail → handleLine → handleEvent pipeline (server.go:620-792) is generic apart from two Valheim rules: the PeerCount/JoinCode keep-awake block (758-771) and the Steam-login overdue rule (707-723, synthesising ServerReady). Both become adapter hooks: a presence source (log, probe count, or none) and a ready fallback. A probe (RCON/REST/query) can feed counts the same way PeerCount does today.

JoinInfo/joinSettingsLocked (status.go:65-77, 249-259) work by 'the values the running server started with', which generalises. The adapter provides a 'how friends join' description (address/port, password, code, client hint). Status could keep its top-level fields as the Valheim instance (for the old panel and the update handshake) and add a per-instance list.

Discord: discordPost{link, text(), done()} and announceLocked's 'announce key' (code or 'online') idea are generic. The adapter supplies the online text (join hint, mods) and the stop wording. Webhook and channel become per instance, falling back to the main one, and the queue becomes per webhook to keep ordering.

Records: eventsFromLog(path, accounts) (records.go:143-180) only needs a parser factory. recordsData becomes one per game, with its own Posted. dailyText (records.go:263-323) needs per-game wording and a 'deaths available' capability (presence kinds: names / count-only / none).

Reminders: played{Game, Mods, Password} (reminder.go:21-25) and remind() form a generic 'what changed since you last played' model. The adapter provides the version source (log line or install manifest) and the client-mod list, which is empty for most games.

Other per-game hooks: argsKey(s, saveDir) (server.go:169-180) becomes an adapter 'launch fingerprint' for NeedsRestart (status.go:202). exitHint (server.go:334-348) becomes adapter-supplied hint matchers. prepareMods/mods.Env become an optional mods capability. checksLoop/FixFirewall per exe (status.go:352-405) become adapter-declared firewall program and ports. The port check (server.go:258) becomes adapter-declared port roles (TCP/UDP), checked across all instances.

The adapter contract for my part, in total: identity; OS support; installer and installed/version; a launch plan (exe, args, env, cwd, save dir, log path or capture); port roles; settings validation; ready detection plus fallback; stop chain plus timeouts plus save signal; log parser/tracker and noise filter; presence kind and probe; join info and Discord texts; exit hints; restart fingerprint; adoption matcher and run-file name; whether deaths and records apply; optional mods.

ring[T] (rings.go) is reusable for a per-instance log ring. Activity (rings.go:16-22) can gain an omitempty game field without breaking activity.json for old builds. The Options test hooks (Installer, NewInstaller, RestartDelay, SampleInterval, DiscordURL) extend to per-game fakes, and cmd/fakevalheim becomes a fakeserver with personalities.
risks: runtime.json must remain Valheim's run file at the data root with the same shape (manager.go:596-618; server.go:503-522). After a rollback the old build adopts Valheim through it. If an old build only finds Valheim by FindByExe, it adopts with runInfo{}: Announced is empty, so it re-posts the join code in Discord (server.go:670-676). Port is 0, so it falls back to current settings (status.go:255-257). Players' mods are unknown. Other games' run files must use another name or place. Added fields must be omitempty, which old builds ignore since json.Unmarshal drops unknown keys.

Shared legacy files are read by old builds: players.json, records.json, lastplayed.json, activity.json, stats.json, history.json (manager.go:469-546; records.go:34-63; reminder.go:112-133). Writing other games' players, deaths or samples into them makes a rolled-back build show or post them as Valheim's. For example, the daily 'died the most' post would include Minecraft deaths, and KnownPlayers would mix games. Keep other games in their own files and keep Valheim's semantics unchanged.

<data>/logs/server-*.log is treated as Valheim's by three code paths (also in old builds): pruneLogs deletes all but the newest 30 (server.go:795-804), backfillRecords parses them with the Valheim parser (records.go:111-139), and newestLog serves one for download (manager.go:456-463). Other games' logs must live elsewhere. records.json Runs is keyed by the log's basename (records.go:91-95), so per-game records need separate maps or files to avoid same-second name collisions.

Update and rollback timing: New() runs before the web server listens and Start()/adoptRunning run right after (main.go:141, 165-171). The updater counts a build as working only if GET /api/status answers within about a minute (main.go:299-361), so migrations must stay O(1) in New(). Status() holds m.mu while doing disk and network-interface work on every poll: os.Stat of the exe, reading the SteamCMD manifest, net.Interfaces (status.go:129-243). Repeating that for 11 games can slow the 2-3 s poll and the handshake. A killed new build (waitStarted) may already have written new files, which the old build must tolerate.

Takeover across an update: an app update that restarts while servers run relies on adoption (update.go:232; manager.go:296-315). Stdin-controlled games can't be stopped gracefully after adoption without the planned keeper. Announced/codePending handling (manager.go:337-348; server.go:429-433, 489-497) must stay per run, or join codes are re-posted or lost. noteUpdate's 'updated' must keep stopped games stopped. busyLocked must cover every instance's job (update.go:79-89).

Adoption by exe path (server.go:231-237, 519-521): for servers hosted by java or dotnet (Minecraft, Necesse, Vintage Story, Zomboid), FindByExe would match unrelated or sibling processes unless the app runs its own private runtime copy per game. A future second instance of the same game would adopt its sibling. The ±2 s start-time guard (server.go:510) depends on per-OS procStartTime precision.

Windows stop: Interrupt attaches to the server's hidden console, sends CTRL_C_EVENT to process group 0 and sleeps 1 s under consoleMu (platform/proc_windows.go:113-134). Stops of several games are therefore serialised, so Hibernate stopping all games takes N x (1 s + save). Any process sharing that console receives the Ctrl+C too, so games must never share a console. A server started by an elevated copy can't be killed (server.go:121-124). On Unix, Interrupt is SIGINT, and an adopted process's exit code is -1 (proc_unix.go:80-95, 127), so the 'expected exit' logic depends on run.stopping or the tracker's Stopping (server.go:544), which each game's parser must provide.

tail keeps one handle on the log path and only handles truncation, never a rename followed by a new file (server.go:633-642). A game that rotates its log mid-run would go silent. On Windows, Go's os.Open does not share delete access, so the held handle may also block a game's own log rename or delete (likely relevant for log4j-based Minecraft).

Ports: only the base UDP port is checked, and only against already-bound sockets (server.go:258). Valheim's port+1, TCP-only games and two games starting at once (a race before either binds) aren't covered. The decisions require automatic clash-free ports that never move owner-chosen ones, so the app must reserve ports across instances itself.

Global counters would cross-contaminate games: the crash budget of 3 in 15 min (server.go:561-568), idleSince reset by any job or join (jobs.go:98; server.go:754, 765) and the 15-min keepAwakeUntil hold (server.go:768-770). The decisions want per-game auto-stop after 1 h and machine sleep only when nobody plays any game, so per-game idle and machine idle must be separate clocks. In R1, an old-style single run must not let the computer sleep while another game runs (power.go:395-475 relies on m.run).

Discord: the queue holds 16 posts and drops when full (discord.go:252-261; manager.go:225). It posts serially with up to 100 s of retries per post (discord.go:280-298), and Close flushes only 5 s (manager.go:331). Bursts with several games (sleep stopping all, wake starting several) can drop or delay posts. The 'stopped never overtakes online' ordering holds only within one queue.

Tests reach into single-run internals: m.run, m.run.proc/ready/replaying/info, m.job, m.jobSeq, m.recs and handleLine (manager_test.go:135-139, 543, 570, 656, 681, 735, 770, 779, 863-867, 1072; discord_test.go:262, 384; modscode_test.go:85; records_test.go:242, 258, 336). They expect runtime.json at the data root (manager_test.go:240, 590-594, 618-641), and every test needs the Valheim fake built in TestMain (manager_test.go:28-48). The R2 gate requires all existing tests green, so the refactor needs compatible accessors or careful test rewrites. TestRealServer covers only Valheim.

hashPassword's salt 'valheim-easy-server:' and lastplayed.json's 'Mods != nil' validity check (reminder.go:27-30, 112-121) are compatibility points. Changing the salt or shape would make every reminder say 'use the new password' once, or drop the saved state. The same applies to the Status/ExitInfo/JoinInfo/Job JSON shapes, which the old panel (still shipped in R2) and the tray read; the update handshake only needs HTTP 200 from /api/status.

summary:
Valheim is hard-coded throughout internal/manager and internal/logparse, and the manager is built around exactly one process. Each Valheim detail is a direct call or string: SteamCMD app 896660, the valheim_server exe/args/env (SteamAppId=892970, macOS DYLD path), BepInEx/Thunderstore mods, the r2modman/Gale share code, crossplay join codes, Ctrl+C save-and-stop with 'World saved' progress, Valheim log formats and texts, Steam/PlayFab platform ids, and death-centric records. internal/logparse is entirely a Valheim log parser.

The single-server assumption sits in a few places: the Manager fields (run, job, loadWait, lastExit, crashes, known, lastPlayed, recs, idleSince, resumeOnWake, logs ring), the single job slot, the single runtime.json, adoption of procs[0] by exe, the one Discord queue, one players/records/lastplayed file each, one Status, and every public action and API route taking no game.

Good seams already exist: serverRun is a per-run object, runInfo is a persisted run record, the job machinery is generic, steamcmd.Installer and platform.Proc abstract installing and processes, logparse.Activity and records.Event are game-neutral, the tail/handle pipeline is nearly generic, and the Discord announce-key model and played/remind() are reusable. A per-instance struct holding today's single-run fields, plus a game adapter, covers this part. The adapter provides: installer and version, launch plan, port roles, ready detection and fallback, stop chain, log parser/tracker, presence source, join info and texts, exit hints, restart fingerprint, adoption matcher and capabilities (deaths, mods).

The main risks:
- Keep runtime.json and the other legacy files Valheim-only and unchanged in shape, so rollback and takeover keep working.
- Keep other games' logs out of logs/server-*.log.
- Keep migrations O(1) and Status() fast within the updater's one-minute handshake.
- Adoption by exe path is ambiguous for java/dotnet servers and for a second instance of a game.
- Windows Ctrl+C stops run one at a time through a shared console lock.
- The log tailer doesn't follow rotated logs.
- Global crash, idle and keep-awake counters would mix games.
- The 16-post Discord queue can drop posts in bursts.
- Many tests read m.run, m.job and runtime.json directly.

Its mods.prune deletes installed packages missing from its catalog (mods.go:314-339), which a newer build re-downloads later. Adding Valheim catalog entries is therefore lossy across a rollback.

The Doorstop dylib exists only in release builds (doorstop.go, build.yml:258); otherwise BepInExPack's copy needs the newest macOS, and Env returns nil, meaning no mods, when no library is found (mods.go:403-406). Package-level test hooks (exportRetryDelay and zipping at library.go:566-570, renameFile at 709) are globals, so parallel tests of several instances can interfere.

The steamcmd tests are tagged !windows (steamcmd_test.go:1), so Windows SteamCMD has no test.

Auto-update and takeover: NewUpload and startJob refuse while m.app.updating (worldio.go:48-56; jobs.go:86-89). busyLocked counts uploads younger than 2 h (update.go:80-90). makeModsCode skips its Discord post when closing so the build that takes over posts it from runtime.json (modscode.go:41). Per-instance code must keep these checks app-wide and keep runtime.json as Valheim's run file.

Limits are global or Valheim-sized: MaxUploadBytes is 16 GB (importer.go:393; web/api.go:375 MaxBytesReader), the disk-space message says about 2 GB (steamcmd.go:298), and maxZip is 512 MB (mods.go:179). Satisfactory (~15.5 GB) and Windrose (~35 GB) need per-game sizes in the texts and the Add-a-game check.
summary: The three packages and three manager files are almost entirely Valheim-specific, but they already have usable seams. internal/worlds hard-codes Valheim's save formats: .fwl/.db pairs, 1.0 folders with _main.N.fwl2 and chunks, `_backup_` copies, .old previous saves, the binary metadata codec, the IronGate/Valheim save paths, Steam Cloud app 892970, and Valheim naming rules through config.WorldNameProblem. Its transactional engine does not depend on the format: zip backups, the fingerprinted export, set-aside/undo replace, restore, import with a busy callback, and upload/extract safety. internal/mods is a BepInEx 5 installer for Valheim's Thunderstore community: a Valheim catalog, BepInExPack_Valheim, winhttp.dll on Windows, Doorstop env with valheim_server and linux64 paths, an embedded macOS dylib, the 'Valheim' r2modman profile prefix and a record file in BepInEx. The Thunderstore client itself is community-agnostic. config imports mods to validate world options, so the Valheim catalog is built into settings loading. internal/steamcmd hard-codes AppID 896660 in the arguments, the success regex and the manifest, plus Valheim progress and disk-size texts, but its Installer interface is already game-neutral and swappable. In the manager, worldio.go, settings.go and modscode.go assume one m.run, one job queue, one selected world and one WorldOptions map, one m.paths, Library, installer and modVersions, one uploads map and one localCands, one modscodes.json, and API routes without a game id. summary:
I read the three areas I was given in full: internal/config (config.go, lists.go, secrets.go and the tests), internal/web (server.go, auth.go, api.go and the tests) and the whole panel in internal/web/ui (index.html, manifest, app.css and every JS module). I changed nothing. All paths are relative to /home/user/valheim-easy-server-/.

- **config is Valheim from top to bottom.**
  - One flat Settings struct with Valheim fields and rules: server name, password rules, the 2456/port+1 port rule, world-name rules ("_backup_", 40 characters), world modifiers, Thunderstore mod ids.
  - The exact valheim_server command line, Valheim's three permission list files, and one single-server folder layout.
  - App-wide settings live in the same struct: resting, idle sleep, self-update, Discord and the JetKVM waker.

- **web assumes one server.** It holds one concrete manager. Its routes (/api/server, /api/worlds, /api/settings, /api/lists, /api/stats, /api/logs and the rest) take no game id. /api/status is one Status with one state, one job, one join block, one player list and one process's CPU and memory. The settings POST replaces the whole Settings object. The error shapes and the security guard are generic and reusable as they are.

- **The panel is hard-wired to one Valheim server.**
  - Hash routes have no game segment, and pages keep their data in module-level variables.
  - Actions post without a game id.
  - Valheim text is everywhere: join codes and crossplay, Party.dll and PlayFab, Steam_ ids, "of 10" players, F5/F2, .fwl/.db files and the IronGate folder, Riverheim, Thunderstore/r2modman/Gale, /valheim.
  - The Valheim modifier lists and the password word list are copied from the Go code.

- **Seams for a game adapter.**
  - In config, the pieces of a per-game Plan already exist: ServerArgs, ServerExeName and ResolvePaths. Validation and world options can become per-game schemas; the settings response already sends the modifier lists, but the panel ignores them. The player lists can become a per-game interface.
  - In the panel, the page modules, the data-action click handling and dom.js/charts.js/download.js carry over.
  - Each adapter would also need to supply a per-game descriptor; the full list of fields is in the seams entries.

- **Biggest risks.**
  - **settings.json rollback:** an older build reading a file with Valheim fields missing generates a new random password and the world "Midgard", and its save drops any keys it doesn't know.
  - **Whole-object settings POST:** it can blank any new field that an old open panel doesn't send back.
  - **Update handshake and old panels:** they need /api/status to answer and its top-level fields and app.version to stay.
  - **Tests that pin Valheim:** they include the "Valheim Easy Server" title check, so the rename breaks it.
  - **Field-error routing:** errors are keyed by bare names like "port" and "password", and any error opens the single Settings page.
  - **Copied constants:** the panel's modifier and password lists will drift from the Go code.
  - **Browser storage:** remembered panel state is lost when the panel's port or host name changes, so stars and the sidebar's open/closed lists should be stored by the app.
  - **Single job:** only one job runs at a time across the whole app, and old panels depend on that.
  - **Windows/macOS:** file permissions, renaming files a running server has open, and wording that branches on the platform.

Until then an OLD waker sends random 6-byte tags and only /valheim, so a new app must treat a legacy tag as Valheim. After rollback, a NEW waker's /minecraft packet reaches an old app, which starts Valheim, until upkeep reinstalls the old waker. Keep game info after byte 108 (wol.go:47) so old apps see a plain tag. An old waker binary must tolerate a new config.json (unknown JSON fields are ignored, but Config.Query and Name stay required for /valheim).

Changing the commands per star toggle means a full binary copy and restart through jetkvm.Install. A failure there is only shown in WakerView.Problem.

Webhooks allow about 5 posts per 2 s each. The single queue of 16 drops posts silently (discord.go:252-259) once 11 games post at 23:59 or all stop for sleep. The Windrose "any message in the channel" rule needs message events (gateway intent GUILD_MESSAGES, 1<<9, today only GUILDS = 1, waker/discord.go:165) or REST reads with VIEW_CHANNEL/READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY. The invite asks for permissions "0" (bot.go:187), so existing bots may need re-inviting.

Discord memory-short reply: today the waker answers the interaction itself and only edits it after an A2S answer or a 10-minute timeout (bot.go:428-480). The app has no way back to the waker except SSH. "Not enough memory, here's what's running" needs either the app to edit the interaction (it would need the interaction token, e.g. carried in the wake packet) or the app to post in the game's channel through the webhook.

Wake ordering race: after a Discord wake the computer reports WakeByDevice. wokenOnPurpose (power.go:371-390) can fire before the first repeated tagged packet is heard (packets every 10 s, bot.go:123-125; wake cause asked every 5 s, power.go:267). It then schedules the previous games to resume in 20 s. Decisions say a Discord wake for one game starts only that game, so the resume must be cancelled or re-checked when a tagged request arrives. TestResumeOwedThroughTimerWakes, TestKVMWakeKeepsAwake and TestLongDarkWakeThenFullWake (power_test.go) pin the current resume semantics.

Idle vs auto-stop interplay: computer sleep (IdleMinutes default 60, config.go:153) and per-game auto-stop (default 1 h) fire at about the same time. If sleep wins, Hibernate stops the idle game and marks it to resume on wake (power.go:73), so it comes back after wake. If auto-stop wins, it does not. Games without a player signal (Windrose) would either never let the computer sleep or let it sleep with players on. Valheim's PeerCount hold (server.go:760-770) is a safety net other games lack.

Process usage: sample() measures one proc (power.go:216-229). Several servers run a launcher whose child does the work: Project Zomboid .bat→java, Palworld PalServer.exe→…Shipping-Cmd.exe, Satisfactory FactoryServer.exe→UnrealServer…exe, plus .NET/Java hosts. The memory bar, the memory check and the stats would read the launcher's small RSS unless the whole process tree is summed.

Windows console stop: Interrupt attaches to the server's console and sends CTRL_C_EVENT to process group 0, i.e. everything on that console (platform/proc_windows.go:113-133). The app ignores Ctrl+C for that reason (main.go:181-193). With several game processes, if two share a console, stopping one interrupts the other. Other games stop differently (stdin "stop"/"exit", RCON, REST).

Records/log collisions: all logs share dataDir/logs and the "server-<second>.log" name (server.go:266). records.json keys by base name (records.go:90-97). backfillRecords would run the Valheim parser on other games' logs if they match the glob (records.go:111). Keep Valheim's existing records.json keys and Posted, or yesterday's Valheim daily post repeats or vanishes after migration (records.go:226-240; first run sets Posted to yesterday, 53).

Reminder hash salt "valheim-easy-server:" (reminder.go:28) and lastplayed.json must stay as they are. Changing the salt or the format makes every player see "use the new password" or "update Valheim" after the update.

"In Valheim, go to Join Game…"), records_test.go TestDailyText/TestDailyDiscordPost ("vikings"), waker/bot_test.go (command "valheim", replies, Query "192.0.2.20:2457", TestLoadConfig), manager/waker_test.go:127-128 (exact waker.Config equality, s.Port+1, Setup.Name), wakesignal_test.go:64 (activity text), jetkvm_test.go and fakekvm (file names, "ok Valheim Bot"), main_test.go (relaunchArgs, stopAndWait fakeStopper using manager.Job/State, resolveDataDir).

Menu items are created once in ready(), so a changing game list must use Show/Hide or submenus. The "Hibernate computer" label path (main.go:365-370) is dead because hibernation is off (config.go:111 HibernationOffered=false), but RestMode stays persisted.

Windows goes back to sleep about 2 minutes after an unattended wake unless held (power.go:256-260, 342-351). The KVM button while awake: today an untagged packet heard while awake starts Valheim (wakesignal.go:83-96). By decisions it should start only the games that ran before sleep, or nothing. resumeOnWake is used up in wokenOnPurpose, so the meaning "before the computer slept" needs a persisted or remembered set, separate from the resume flag.
summary:
I read all of my part (none of it was changed): main.go, internal/discord, internal/waker (plus cmd/valheim-waker), internal/jetkvm (plus fakekvm and dist), internal/wol, internal/stats, internal/records, internal/tray, and the manager files power.go, discord.go, waker.go, wakesignal.go, records.go and reminder.go. I also read the parts of manager.go, status.go, settings.go, server.go and jobs.go that these depend on.

Valheim is hard-coded in five places in this part:
- **The Discord bot:** the single /valheim command, its replies, and a liveness check that only speaks Steam's A2S query on the game port + 1.
- **The Discord posts:** join code and crossplay, the "In Valheim…" join hint, r2modman/Gale mods, "update Valheim to X" reminders, and "vikings" in the daily post.
- **Records:** built from Valheim-format logs found with the glob server-*.log.
- **Text:** the tray labels and main.go's dialogs.
- **Identifiers:** the data folder names, the single-instance lock, and the valheim-waker paths and script on the JetKVM. Decisions say these must keep working. main.go:462 uses appName as both the visible name and the Downloads/Desktop data subfolder, so it has to be split before the rename.

Everything assumes one server. The Manager holds one run and one job, one resume-after-wake flag, one set of idle timers, and one wake tag and start time. The waker holds one waking state, one command, one name, one query address and one Discord server. Discord has one webhook, one serial queue of 16 that drops posts when full, and one daily-post watermark. Each data file holds one server: runtime.json, records.json (keyed by log name, so two games' logs could collide), stats.json, history.json and lastplayed.json. Usage sampling reads one process. The tray and stopAndWait start and stop one server.

Good seams:
- discord.Post/Guild/Problem/Escape are already generic, and the webhook's JSON also carries the channel id.
- Each queued Discord post already carries its own link.
- The waker's query function can be replaced, and Discord's bulk command overwrite replaces the whole set.
- The WoL packet has room for a game id after byte 108, which old apps ignore.
- The jetkvm transport, records.Compute, stats History/ByPlayers, the computer-level sleep and wake logic in power.go, and main.go's serverStopper interface can all be reused.

For this part, a game adapter needs to provide:
- the slash-command name and Discord wording;
- a liveness probe: A2S, Minecraft's status ping, TCP connect, or none;
- query and game ports;
- the join and leave signal, and whether deaths are known;
- the log folder, file pattern and parser;
- a version and mods for reminders, if any;
- its process tree for usage;
- its stop method.

Highest risks:
- **Update and rollback:** the old app needs a 200 from /api/status within a minute or it rolls back, so slow migrations before the panel opens trigger it. Migrations must be additive so an older version can still read the folder. A new command-line flag would make a rolled-back version exit.
- **Waker and app out of step:** until the JetKVM waker is reinstalled, the new app must treat old wake tags as Valheim; after a rollback, an old app would start Valheim for /minecraft. upkeepWaker's `setup == file.Setup` comparison stops compiling once the setup holds lists.
- **Wake race:** waking the computer for one game from Discord can also restart the games that ran before sleep, which the decisions forbid.
- **Idle and memory:** the per-game auto-stop and computer sleep timers interact, Windrose has no player signal, and servers started through a launcher under-report memory.
- **Windows stop:** the stop signal goes to everything on the server's console.
- **Discord:** rate limits, and the bot's intents and invite permissions, which the Windrose rule needs changed.
- **Tests:** the Discord, waker, JetKVM, records and main tests check the current text and structure exactly.

risks: Firewall compat (Windows): old builds' Allow deletes every 'Valheim Easy Server - *' rule and all rules for program=$server/$app (winparse.go:41,43,45). New games' rules need a different prefix and must never share a program path with the Valheim server or the app. Valheim's names (sha8 fingerprint winparse.go:24, legacy names desktop_windows.go:176-181) must stay byte-identical, so FirewallReady still says OK after an update and after a rollback.

No golden tests freeze the identity constants: fwRules, runValue, the mutex name, the temp lock, launchLabel, ExeName, Repo/RepoID. The tests use the constants themselves (selfupdate_test.go:26-29,60-61; winparse_test.go:13-44; TestLaunchAgentPlist uses com.example.app, macparse_test.go:173-174), so a rename passes unit tests. Only CI's hard-coded PowerShell (build.yml:132-140) would catch an ExeName change on Windows; nothing would on Mac. Add golden tests in R1.

Admin command length: the inline elevated command must stay under 2048 characters (pscommand.go:51). TestFirewallScriptFitsLongPaths (winparse_test.go:58-81) and TestAdminCommandShortScript (psadmin_test.go:37-46) assume the 2-path Valheim script fits inline. More rules move to the hashed temp-file path (pscommand.go:60-78), whose cleanup only removes files older than 1 h (power_windows.go:117-122); test expectations change.

Swap removes exe.old before renaming (selfupdate.go:223-234) and Restore renames exe.old over exe (:249-251). On Windows, any process still running from exe or exe.old (a keeper or helper) makes the next update or the rollback fail after 10×300 ms retries (:237-246). Helpers must run from their own copy (e.g. <data>/bin/keeper-<sha8>), which CleanUp (exe.new only, :253-256) leaves alone.

Mac self-update replaces only Contents/MacOS/ValheimEasyServer (build.yml:248, selfupdate.go:38). Info.plist (CFBundleName "Valheim Easy Server", BUILD_NUMBER), the bundle folder name and the icon never change on installed Macs, so 'Easy Game Server' only shows inside the panel for existing Mac users. If new zips rename the .app, users get two bundles sharing ~/Library/Application Support/ValheimEasyServer: SingleInstance protects the data, but LaunchOnLogin compares the exe path (desktop_darwin.go:30-48), so it reads 'off' for the new copy while the LaunchAgent keeps starting the old one.

Branch builds update themselves: github.run_number counts every push/PR run of build.yml on any branch (build.yml:3-5,78,94), and branch artifacts are built with -X main.build=N. An R2/R3 test copy from the multigame branch will auto-update to the next default-branch release with a higher N, which is a silent rollback to pre-R2 code during the owner's 3-day test. Data written by R2 must survive that, or test copies must be built without main.build. Never rename build.yml: it resets N, and installed copies only take a higher N (selfupdate.go:140).

CI gaps and brittleness: smoke tests grep "Valheim Easy Server" (build.yml:106,278; index.html:8), so the R3 rename breaks them. They also require top-level state "not_installed" and "platform":"darwin" (:104,:276-277), which R2's virtual Valheim must keep. The self-update test builds 'build 1' from the same commit (:124), not from a real old release; it runs no server (no takeover check) and checks app.build/app.failed/activity text "The app was updated to build N*" plus POST /api/app/update with X-VES (:152-178). There is no Mac self-update test and no test of rolling back to a real release. The release job needs linux, windows and mac (:294); adding real-server cells there would block releases on multi-GB downloads. node --check only covers internal/web/ui/assets/*.js (:36), not subfolders.

Mac coverage: CI runs macos-15-intel (build.yml:196, real-server.yml:22), but the owner's Mac Pro runs macOS 12. Runtimes (Temurin, Necesse's bundled JRE, Terraria's MonoKickstart) aren't proven on 12, and Apple-silicon/Rosetta paths aren't tested. Go must stay at 1.26 for macOS 12 (go.mod:3-5, minos check build.yml:230-239). Runner disk for Satisfactory (~15.5 GB) and Windrose (~35 GB) needs checking; Enshrouded and Windrose need Windows cells.

Windows Ctrl+C: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_C_EVENT, 0) reaches every process attached to that console (proc_windows.go:118-124), so a keeper sharing the game's console gets it too. The app ignores Ctrl+C for about 1 s around it (:122-128). Terraria doesn't save on Ctrl+C, so an Interrupt-only stop would lose its world. TestInterruptReachesConsoleProgram (platform_windows_test.go:41-108) is the only real Ctrl+C test: keep it and add keeper/stdin equivalents.

Adoption edge cases: Windows OpenProc falls back to SYNCHRONIZE|QUERY_LIMITED on access denied (proc_windows.go:70-74), after which Kill and Usage fail. Unix adopted processes report exit code -1 (proc_unix.go:89-91), so after a takeover a crash can't be told from a clean stop. This matters for per-game crash restart and auto-stop accounting.

Flags and handshake: relaunchArgs passes the running app's args to the next build (main.go:270-295), and the Run entry/LaunchAgent pass --background (status.go:409). A new flag would make an older build exit after a rollback, so use EGS_DEV_* environment variables. --dev-fake-server (main.go:55,134) is wired to the single Valheim exe name. .instance.json {port} plus GET /api/status 200 (main.go:340-360, 547-560) and update.json {from,to,title,failed} (manager/update.go:43-53) are the rollback contract.

Waker compatibility: names and paths (/userdata/valheim-waker, S99valheim-waker, /tmp/valheim-waker.json; main.go:26-27, jetkvm.go:109,199-223) must stay. The waker's version equals the app's (build.yml:80-81), so every app update reinstalls it. After a rollback the old app reinstalls the single-/valheim waker with the old config: new Config fields must be optional, and the old waker's PUT [valheim] (bot.go:296) wipes the per-game commands, which is acceptable. The new waker must accept an old config. Release builds need the waker built into internal/jetkvm/dist before `go build` (only a README is committed).

fakevalheim cost and fidelity: 150 MB plus 60 MB per player and per-player CPU burn (main.go:133,351,440-453). Several fakes in parallel on CI (Linux runs with -race, build.yml:55) cost memory and time, and memory-check tests need controllable reported memory rather than real ballast. Its password rule ignores the server name (main.go:135-139 vs README:256), and it never binds its port, so tests built on it can't catch those cases.

Docs drift to fix while rewriting: README:312 says Go 1.27+, but go.mod:5 is 1.26.10 and build.yml:236 says build with Go 1.26. README:319 says CI tests 'Linux and Windows' (Mac too). README:10 says 'five short steps', READ-ME-FIRST.txt:42 says 'six'. README:247,274 tell users to rename ValheimEasyServer.exe.old, so those names must stay. The READ-ME-FIRST files ship inside the zips (build.yml:187,259). Release notes' first line comes from the head commit message (build.yml:309-317, selfupdate.go:128) and shows in the app's activity list, so the R1/R2/R3 gate merge commits need a meaningful first line.
summary:
Scope covered: internal/platform (all OS files and tests), internal/selfupdate, cmd/fakevalheim with its test harness (manager_test.go TestMain, steamcmd.Fake, FAKE_VALHEIM_* env passed through server.go:271), cmd/valheim-waker (plus the internal/waker and internal/jetkvm bits its flags and paths depend on), macapp/Info.plist, .github/workflows/build.yml and real-server.yml, .github/scripts/build-doorstop.sh, README.md and docs/*.

**Platform.** It is mostly game-agnostic and is the natural OS seam: process handles, power, wake, idle, network adapters, usage sampling and desktop integration. The Valheim/single-server spots are:
- **Firewall:** one game exe per call, and the Windows script deletes every 'Valheim Easy Server - *' rule and every rule for the server's program path (winparse.go:15-48), so new games need their own prefix and per-rule port scoping for shared runtimes.
- **Port check:** UDP-only and owner-blind (desktop_windows.go:270, desktop_unix.go:107).
- **KeepAwake:** a single on/off switch (power_windows.go:142, power_darwin.go:41).
- **Process matching and stopping:** FindByExe matches by path only, Usage and signals cover one PID, and there is no stdin/stdout capture. That's why the keeper and process-tree/group helpers are needed.
- **Missing pieces:** TCP and owner-aware port checks, known folders, OS/arch/Rosetta facts, elevated installs that wait for the result, and gateway discovery.
- **Identity names to freeze with golden tests (none exist today):** Run value, mutex, lock file, admin script prefix, LaunchAgent label.

**selfupdate.** Game-agnostic, but its identity constants (Repo, RepoID, ExeName) and the Swap/.old/Restore contract (selfupdate.go:223-251) constrain helper processes. Two release risks:
- Mac updates replace only the binary, so Info.plist names never change on installed Macs.
- Branch builds carry main.build=N from a shared run_number, so an owner's R2 test copy will auto-update back to a newer default-branch release.

**fakevalheim.** Entirely Valheim (args, log lines, world format, SteamIDs, password rule). It is configured through process-wide env vars, which forces serial tests, and it opens no sockets and reads no stdin. Its core (arg loop, log writer, scripts, ballast, signal-save) can become the multi-personality fakeserver.

**Waker.** One /valheim command with one MAC, Query, Name and Guild. Registration PUTs the guild's whole command list (bot.go:287-296), which helps rollback; the paths and names must stay.

**CI.**
- Smoke tests grep "Valheim Easy Server" and the top-level state (build.yml:104-106, 276-278).
- The self-update test runs no server and builds its 'old' copy from the same commit.
- There is no Mac update test.
- Mac CI is macOS 15 Intel, not the owner's macOS 12.
- real-server.yml is Valheim-only and needs a game × OS matrix with on-demand inputs.

**Docs.** README and both READ-ME-FIRST files are Valheim throughout and contain some drift: the Go version (README says 1.27, go.mod says 1.26), the OSes CI tests on, and the tutorial step count.
